AAAS.fn: Plays a role in the normal development of the peripheral and central nervous system.

AAMP.fn: Plays a role in angiogenesis and cell migration. In smooth muscle cell migration, may act through the RhoA pathway. .

AAR2.fn: Component of the U5 snRNP complex that is required for spliceosome assembly and for pre-mRNA splicing. .

AARS2.fn: Catalyzes the attachment of alanine to tRNA(Ala) in a two-step reaction: alanine is first activated by ATP to form Ala-AMP and then transferred to the acceptor end of tRNA(Ala). Also edits incorrectly charged tRNA(Ala) via its editing domain.

AASDHPPT.fn: Catalyzes the post-translational modification of target proteins by phosphopantetheine.

AATF.fn: Part of the small subunit (SSU) processome, first precursor of the small eukaryotic ribosomal subunit.

ABCB10.protein: ATP-binding cassette sub-family B member 10, mitochondrial
ABCB10.fn: ATP-dependent transporter located in the mitochondrial inner membrane that catalyzes the export of biliverdin from the mitochondrial matrix, and plays a crucial role in hemoglobin synthesis and antioxidative stress.

ABCB7.fn: Exports glutathione-coordinated iron-sulfur clusters such as [2Fe-2S]-(GS)4 cluster from the mitochondria to the cytosol in an ATP-dependent manner allowing the assembly of the cytosolic iron-sulfur (Fe/S) cluster-containing proteins and participates in iron h

ABCE1.fn: Nucleoside-triphosphatase (NTPase) involved in ribosome recycling by mediating ribosome disassembly. Able to hydrolyze ATP, GTP, UTP and CTP. Splits ribosomes into free 60S subunits and tRNA- and mRNA-bound 40S subunits.

ABCF1.fn: Isoform 2 is required for efficient Cap- and IRES-mediated mRNA translation initiation. Isoform 2 is not involved in the ribosome biogenesis. .

ABCG1.fn: Catalyzes the efflux of phospholipids such as sphingomyelin, cholesterol and its oxygenated derivatives like 7beta-hydroxycholesterol and this transport is coupled to hydrolysis of ATP. The lipid efflux is ALB-dependent.

ABHD11.fn: Catalyzes the hydrolysis of diacylglycerol in vitro and may function as a key regulator in lipid metabolism, namely by regulating the intracellular levels of diacylglycerol.

ABHD17A.fn: Hydrolyzes fatty acids from S-acylated cysteine residues in proteins. Has depalmitoylating activity towards NRAS. Has depalmitoylating activity towards DLG4/PSD95. May have depalmitoylating activity towards MAP6 (By similarity). .

ABL1.fn: Non-receptor tyrosine-protein kinase that plays a role in many key processes linked to cell growth and survival such as cytoskeleton remodeling in response to extracellular stimuli, cell motility and adhesion, receptor endocytosis, autophagy, DNA damage respon

ABT1.fn: Could be a novel TATA-binding protein (TBP) which can function as a basal transcription activator. Can act as a regulator of basal transcription for class II genes (By similarity). .

ACD.fn: Component of the shelterin complex (telosome) that is involved in the regulation of telomere length and protection. Shelterin associates with arrays of double-stranded TTAGGG repeats added by telomerase and protects chromosome ends.

ACIN1.protein: Apoptotic chromatin condensation inducer in the nucleus
ACIN1.fn: Auxiliary component of the splicing-dependent multiprotein exon junction complex (EJC) deposited at splice junction on mRNAs.

ACOT12.fn: Catalyzes the hydrolysis of acyl-CoAs into free fatty acids and coenzyme A (CoASH), regulating their respective intracellular levels. Preferentially hydrolyzes acetyl-CoA. .

ACSS2.fn: Catalyzes the synthesis of acetyl-CoA from short-chain fatty acids. Acetate is the preferred substrate. Can also utilize propionate with a much lower affinity. Catalyzes the conversion of lactate into lactoyl-CoA.

ACTB.fn: Actin is a highly conserved protein that polymerizes to produce filaments that form cross-linked networks in the cytoplasm of cells.

ACTL6A.fn: Involved in transcriptional activation and repression of select genes by chromatin remodeling (alteration of DNA-nucleosome topology).

ACTR10.fn: Part of the dynactin complex that activates the molecular motor dynein for ultra-processive transport along microtubules. .

ACTR1A.fn: Part of the ACTR1A/ACTB filament around which the dynactin complex is built. The dynactin multiprotein complex activates the molecular motor dynein for ultra-processive transport along microtubules. .

ACTR1B.fn: Component of a multi-subunit complex involved in microtubule based vesicle motility. It is associated with the centrosome.

ACTR2.fn: ATP-binding component of the Arp2/3 complex, a multiprotein complex that mediates actin polymerization upon stimulation by nucleation-promoting factor (NPF).

ACTR3.fn: ATP-binding component of the Arp2/3 complex, a multiprotein complex that mediates actin polymerization upon stimulation by nucleation-promoting factor (NPF).

ACTR5.fn: Proposed core component of the chromatin remodeling INO80 complex which is involved in transcriptional regulation, DNA replication and probably DNA repair. Involved in DNA double-strand break repair and UV-damage excision repair. .

ACTR6.fn: Required for formation and/or maintenance of proper nucleolar structure and function. Plays a dual role in the regulation of ribosomal DNA (rDNA) transcription (By similarity).

ACTR8.fn: Plays an important role in the functional organization of mitotic chromosomes.

ADAM10.fn: Transmembrane metalloprotease which mediates the ectodomain shedding of a myriad of transmembrane proteins, including adhesion proteins, growth factor precursors and cytokines being essential for development and tissue homeostasis.

ADAT2.protein: tRNA-specific adenosine-34 deaminase catalytic subunit ADAT2
ADAT2.fn: Catalytic subunit of the tRNA-specific adenosine-34 deaminase complex, composed of the ADAT2 catalytic subunit and the ADAT3 regulatory subunit, which deaminates adenosine-34 (the first, also called wobble position of the anticodon) to inosine in many tRNAs.

ADAT3.protein: tRNA-specific adenosine-34 deaminase regulatory subunit ADAT3
ADAT3.fn: Non-catalytic subunit of the tRNA-specific adenosine-34 deaminase complex, composed of the ADAT2 catalytic subunit and the ADAT3 regulatory subunit, which deaminates adenosine-34 (the first, also called wobble position of the anticodon) to inosine in many tRNA

ADNP2.fn: May be involved in transcriptional regulation. May play a role in neuronal function; perhaps involved in protection of brain tissues from oxidative stress. May be involved in erythroid differentiation (By similarity). .

ADRM1.fn: Component of the 26S proteasome, a multiprotein complex involved in the ATP-dependent degradation of ubiquitinated proteins.

ADSL.fn: Catalyzes two non-sequential steps in de novo AMP synthesis: converts (S)-2-(5-amino-1-(5-phospho-D-ribosyl)imidazole-4-carboxamido)succinate (SAICAR) to fumarate plus 5-amino-1-(5-phospho-D-ribosyl)imidazole-4-carboxamide, and thereby also contributes to de n

AFG3L2.protein: Mitochondrial inner membrane m-AAA protease component AFG3L2
AFG3L2.fn: Catalytic component of the m-AAA protease, a protease that plays a key role in proteostasis of inner mitochondrial membrane proteins, and which is essential for axonal and neuron development.

AGBL5.fn: Metallocarboxypeptidase that mediates deglutamylation of tubulin and non-tubulin target proteins.

AHCTF1.fn: Required for the assembly of a functional nuclear pore complex (NPC) on the surface of chromosomes as nuclei form at the end of mitosis. May initiate NPC assembly by binding to chromatin and recruiting the Nup107-160 subcomplex of the NPC.

AHCY.fn: Catalyzes the hydrolysis of S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine to form adenosine and homocysteine. Binds copper ions (By similarity). .

AIFM1.fn: Functions both as NADH oxidoreductase and as regulator of apoptosis.

AKIRIN2.fn: Molecular adapter that acts as a bridge between a variety of multiprotein complexes, and which is involved in embryonic development, immunity, myogenesis and brain development.

AKT1.fn: AKT1 is one of 3 closely related serine/threonine-protein kinases (AKT1, AKT2 and AKT3) called the AKT kinase, and which regulate many processes including metabolism, proliferation, cell survival, growth and angiogenesis.

ALDOA.fn: Catalyzes the reversible conversion of beta-D-fructose 1,6-bisphosphate (FBP) into two triose phosphate and plays a key role in glycolysis and gluconeogenesis. In addition, also functions as a scaffolding protein (By similarity).

ALG1.fn: Mannosyltransferase that operates in the biosynthetic pathway of dolichol-linked oligosaccharides, the glycan precursors employed in protein asparagine (N)-glycosylation.

ALG11.fn: GDP-Man:Man(3)GlcNAc(2)-PP-Dol alpha-1,2-mannosyltransferase that operates in the biosynthetic pathway of dolichol-linked oligosaccharides, the glycan precursors employed in protein asparagine (N)-glycosylation.

ALG13.fn: Catalytic subunit of the UDP-N-acetylglucosamine transferase complex that operates in the biosynthetic pathway of dolichol-linked oligosaccharides, the glycan precursors employed in protein asparagine (N)-glycosylation.

ALG14.fn: Part of the UDP-N-acetylglucosamine transferase complex that operates in the biosynthetic pathway of dolichol-linked oligosaccharides, the glycan precursors employed in protein asparagine (N)-glycosylation.

ALG2.fn: Mannosyltransferase that operates in the biosynthetic pathway of dolichol-linked oligosaccharides, the glycan precursors employed in protein asparagine (N)-glycosylation.

ALYREF.fn: Functions as an mRNA export adapter; component of the transcription/export (TREX) complex which is thought to couple mRNA transcription, processing and nuclear export, and specifically associates with spliced mRNA and not with unspliced pre-mRNA.

ANAPC1.fn: Component of the anaphase promoting complex/cyclosome (APC/C), a cell cycle-regulated E3 ubiquitin ligase that controls progression through the cell cycle.

ANAPC10.fn: Component of the anaphase promoting complex/cyclosome (APC/C), a cell cycle-regulated E3 ubiquitin ligase that controls progression through the cell cycle.

ANAPC11.fn: Component of the anaphase promoting complex/cyclosome (APC/C), a cell cycle-regulated E3 ubiquitin ligase that controls progression through the cell cycle. Together with ANAPC2, forms the catalytic component of the E3 ubiquitin ligase complex.

ANAPC13.fn: Component of the anaphase promoting complex/cyclosome (APC/C), a cell cycle-regulated E3 ubiquitin ligase that controls progression through the cell cycle.

ANAPC15.fn: Component of the anaphase promoting complex/cyclosome (APC/C), a cell cycle-regulated E3 ubiquitin ligase that controls progression through the cell cycle.

ANAPC2.fn: Component of the anaphase promoting complex/cyclosome (APC/C), a cell cycle-regulated E3 ubiquitin ligase that controls progression through the cell cycle.

ANAPC4.fn: Component of the anaphase promoting complex/cyclosome (APC/C), a cell cycle-regulated E3 ubiquitin ligase that controls progression through the cell cycle.

ANAPC5.fn: Component of the anaphase promoting complex/cyclosome (APC/C), a cell cycle-regulated E3 ubiquitin ligase that controls progression through the cell cycle.

ANKLE2.protein: Ankyrin repeat and LEM domain-containing protein 2
ANKLE2.fn: Involved in mitotic nuclear envelope reassembly by promoting dephosphorylation of BAF/BANF1 during mitotic exit.

ANKRD11.fn: Chromatin regulator which modulates histone acetylation and gene expression in neural precursor cells (By similarity). May recruit histone deacetylases (HDACs) to the p160 coactivators/nuclear receptor complex to inhibit ligand-dependent transactivation.

ANKRD17.fn: Could play pivotal roles in cell cycle and DNA regulation. Involved in innate immune defense against viruse by positively regulating the viral dsRNA receptors DDX58 and IFIH1 signaling pathways.

ANKRD49.fn: Induces HBG1 expression. May have a role in spermatogenesis where it promotes autophagy in response to serum starvation, via the NF-kappaB pathway (By similarity). .

ANKS6.protein: Ankyrin repeat and SAM domain-containing protein 6

ANLN.fn: Required for cytokinesis. Essential for the structural integrity of the cleavage furrow and for completion of cleavage furrow ingression. Plays a role in bleb assembly during metaphase and anaphase of mitosis.

AP2A1.fn: Component of the adaptor protein complex 2 (AP-2). Adaptor protein complexes function in protein transport via transport vesicles in different membrane traffic pathways.

AP2M1.fn: Component of the adaptor protein complex 2 (AP-2). Adaptor protein complexes function in protein transport via transport vesicles in different membrane traffic pathways.

AP2S1.fn: Component of the adaptor protein complex 2 (AP-2). Adaptor protein complexes function in protein transport via transport vesicles in different membrane traffic pathways.

APC.fn: Tumor suppressor. Promotes rapid degradation of CTNNB1 and participates in Wnt signaling as a negative regulator. APC activity is correlated with its phosphorylation state. Activates the GEF activity of SPATA13 and ARHGEF4.

AQP7.fn: Aquaglyceroporins form homotetrameric transmembrane channels, with each monomer independently mediating glycerol and water transport across the plasma membrane along their osmotic gradient. Could also be permeable to urea.

AQR.fn: Involved in pre-mRNA splicing as component of the spliceosome. Intron-binding spliceosomal protein required to link pre-mRNA splicing and snoRNP (small nucleolar ribonucleoprotein) biogenesis.

ARCN1.fn: Component of the coatomer, a cytosolic protein complex that binds to dilysine motifs and reversibly associates with Golgi non-clathrin-coated vesicles, which further mediate biosynthetic protein transport from the ER, via the Golgi up to the trans Golgi networ

ARF4.fn: GTP-binding protein that functions as an allosteric activator of the cholera toxin catalytic subunit, an ADP-ribosyltransferase. Involved in protein trafficking; may modulate vesicle budding and uncoating within the Golgi apparatus.

ARFRP1.fn: Trans-Golgi-associated GTPase that regulates protein sorting. Controls the targeting of ARL1 and its effector to the trans-Golgi. Required for the lipidation of chylomicrons in the intestine and required for VLDL lipidation in the liver. .

ARGFX.fn: Transcription factor that acts as activator. .

ARGLU1.fn: Dual function regulator of gene expression; regulator of transcription and modulator of alternative splicing. General coactivator of nuclear receptor-induced gene expression, including genes activated by the glucocorticoid receptor NR3C1.

ARHGAP11B.fn: Hominin-specific protein that promotes development and evolutionary expansion of the brain neocortex.

ARHGAP6.fn: GTPase activator for the Rho-type GTPases by converting them to an inactive GDP-bound state. Could regulate the interactions of signaling molecules with the actin cytoskeleton.

ARID1A.fn: Involved in transcriptional activation and repression of select genes by chromatin remodeling (alteration of DNA-nucleosome topology).

ARID3A.fn: Transcription factor which may be involved in the control of cell cycle progression by the RB1/E2F1 pathway and in B-cell differentiation. .

ARID5B.fn: Transcription coactivator that binds to the 5'-AATA[CT]-3' core sequence and plays a key role in adipogenesis and liver development.

ARIH1.fn: E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase, which catalyzes ubiquitination of target proteins together with ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme E2 UBE2L3.

ARL2.fn: Small GTP-binding protein which cycles between an inactive GDP-bound and an active GTP-bound form, and the rate of cycling is regulated by guanine nucleotide exchange factors (GEF) and GTPase-activating proteins (GAP).

ARL4D.fn: Small GTP-binding protein which cycles between an inactive GDP-bound and an active GTP-bound form, and the rate of cycling is regulated by guanine nucleotide exchange factors (GEF) and GTPase-activating proteins (GAP).

ARMC7.fn: As a component of the minor spliceosome, involved in the splicing of U12-type introns in pre-mRNAs. .

ARPC1B.fn: Component of the Arp2/3 complex, a multiprotein complex that mediates actin polymerization upon stimulation by nucleation-promoting factor (NPF).

ARPC2.fn: Actin-binding component of the Arp2/3 complex, a multiprotein complex that mediates actin polymerization upon stimulation by nucleation-promoting factor (NPF).

ARPC3.fn: Component of the Arp2/3 complex, a multiprotein complex that mediates actin polymerization upon stimulation by nucleation-promoting factor (NPF).

ARPC4.fn: Actin-binding component of the Arp2/3 complex, a multiprotein complex that mediates actin polymerization upon stimulation by nucleation-promoting factor (NPF).

ARRB2.fn: Functions in regulating agonist-mediated G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) signaling by mediating both receptor desensitization and resensitization processes.

ASCC3.fn: ATPase involved both in DNA repair and rescue of stalled ribosomes.

ASF1B.fn: Histone chaperone that facilitates histone deposition and histone exchange and removal during nucleosome assembly and disassembly. Cooperates with chromatin assembly factor 1 (CAF-1) to promote replication-dependent chromatin assembly.

ATF4.fn: Transcription factor that binds the cAMP response element (CRE) (consensus: 5'-GTGACGT[AC][AG]-3') and displays two biological functions, as regulator of metabolic and redox processes under normal cellular conditions, and as master transcription factor during

ATF5.fn: Transcription factor that either stimulates or represses gene transcription through binding of different DNA regulatory elements such as cAMP response element (CRE) (consensus: 5'-GTGACGT[AC][AG]-3'), ATF5-specific response element (ARE) (consensus: 5'-C[CT]TC

ATIC.fn: Bifunctional enzyme that catalyzes the last two steps of purine biosynthesis.

ATL2.fn: Atlastin-2 (ATL2) is a membrane-anchored GTPase that mediates the GTP-dependent fusion of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) membranes, maintaining the continuous ER network. It facilitates the formation of three-way junctions where ER tubules intersect.

ATM.fn: Serine/threonine protein kinase which activates checkpoint signaling upon double strand breaks (DSBs), apoptosis and genotoxic stresses such as ionizing ultraviolet A light (UVA), thereby acting as a DNA damage sensor.

ATP11B.fn: Catalytic component of a P4-ATPase flippase complex which catalyzes the hydrolysis of ATP coupled to the transport of aminophospholipids, phosphatidylserines (PS) and phosphatidylethanolamines (PE), from the outer to the inner leaflet of intracellular membrane

ATP1A1.fn: Catalytic subunit of the Na(+)/K(+)-ATPase pump that hydrolyzes ATP to exchange ions across the plasma membrane, exporting 3 Na(+) and importing 2 K(+) per cycle against electrochemical gradients.

ATP2A2.fn: This magnesium-dependent enzyme catalyzes the hydrolysis of ATP coupled with the translocation of calcium from the cytosol to the sarcoplasmic reticulum lumen. Involved in autophagy in response to starvation.

ATP5F1A.protein: ATP synthase F(1) complex subunit alpha, mitochondrial
ATP5F1A.fn: Subunit alpha, of the mitochondrial membrane ATP synthase complex (F(1)F(0) ATP synthase or Complex V) that produces ATP from ADP in the presence of a proton gradient across the membrane which is generated by electron transport complexes of the respiratory cha

ATP5F1B.protein: ATP synthase F(1) complex subunit beta, mitochondrial
ATP5F1B.fn: Catalytic subunit beta, of the mitochondrial membrane ATP synthase complex (F(1)F(0) ATP synthase or Complex V) that produces ATP from ADP in the presence of a proton gradient across the membrane which is generated by electron transport complexes of the respir

ATP5F1C.protein: ATP synthase F(1) complex subunit gamma, mitochondrial
ATP5F1C.fn: Subunit gamma, of the mitochondrial membrane ATP synthase complex (F(1)F(0) ATP synthase or Complex V) that produces ATP from ADP in the presence of a proton gradient across the membrane which is generated by electron transport complexes of the respiratory cha

ATP5ME.protein: ATP synthase F(0) complex subunit e, mitochondrial
ATP5ME.fn: Subunit e, of the mitochondrial membrane ATP synthase complex (F(1)F(0) ATP synthase or Complex V) that produces ATP from ADP in the presence of a proton gradient across the membrane which is generated by electron transport complexes of the respiratory chain.

ATP5MF.protein: ATP synthase F(0) complex subunit f, mitochondrial
ATP5MF.fn: Subunit f, of the mitochondrial membrane ATP synthase complex (F(1)F(0) ATP synthase or Complex V) that produces ATP from ADP in the presence of a proton gradient across the membrane which is generated by electron transport complexes of the respiratory chain.

ATP5PD.protein: ATP synthase peripheral stalk subunit d, mitochondrial
ATP5PD.fn: Subunit d, of the mitochondrial membrane ATP synthase complex (F(1)F(0) ATP synthase or Complex V) that produces ATP from ADP in the presence of a proton gradient across the membrane which is generated by electron transport complexes of the respiratory chain.

ATP5PO.protein: ATP synthase peripheral stalk subunit OSCP, mitochondrial
ATP5PO.fn: Subunit OSCP, of the mitochondrial membrane ATP synthase complex (F(1)F(0) ATP synthase or Complex V) that produces ATP from ADP in the presence of a proton gradient across the membrane which is generated by electron transport complexes of the respiratory chai

ATP6AP1.fn: Accessory subunit of the V0 complex of vacuolar(H+)-ATPase (V-ATPase), a multisubunit enzyme composed of a peripheral complex (V1) that hydrolyzes ATP and a membrane integral complex (V0) that translocates protons.

ATP6AP2.fn: Multifunctional protein which functions as a renin, prorenin cellular receptor and is involved in the assembly of the lysosomal proton-transporting V-type ATPase (V-ATPase) and the acidification of the endo-lysosomal system.

ATP6V0B.protein: V-type proton ATPase 21 kDa proteolipid subunit c''
ATP6V0B.fn: Proton-conducting pore forming subunit of the V0 complex of vacuolar(H+)-ATPase (V-ATPase), a multisubunit enzyme composed of a peripheral complex (V1) that hydrolyzes ATP and a membrane integral complex (V0) that translocates protons.

ATP6V0C.protein: V-type proton ATPase 16 kDa proteolipid subunit c
ATP6V0C.fn: Proton-conducting pore forming subunit of the V0 complex of vacuolar(H+)-ATPase (V-ATPase), a multisubunit enzyme composed of a peripheral complex (V1) that hydrolyzes ATP and a membrane integral complex (V0) that translocates protons.

ATP6V0D1.fn: Subunit of the V0 complex of vacuolar(H+)-ATPase (V-ATPase), a multisubunit enzyme composed of a peripheral complex (V1) that hydrolyzes ATP and a membrane integral complex (V0) that translocates protons.

ATP6V1A.protein: V-type proton ATPase catalytic subunit A
ATP6V1A.fn: Catalytic subunit of the V1 complex of vacuolar(H+)-ATPase (V-ATPase), a multisubunit enzyme composed of a peripheral complex (V1) that hydrolyzes ATP and a membrane integral complex (V0) that translocates protons.

ATP6V1B2.protein: V-type proton ATPase subunit B, brain isoform
ATP6V1B2.fn: Non-catalytic subunit of the V1 complex of vacuolar(H+)-ATPase (V-ATPase), a multisubunit enzyme composed of a peripheral complex (V1) that hydrolyzes ATP and a membrane integral complex (V0) that translocates protons.

ATP6V1C1.fn: Subunit of the V1 complex of vacuolar(H+)-ATPase (V-ATPase), a multisubunit enzyme composed of a peripheral complex (V1) that hydrolyzes ATP and a membrane integral complex (V0) that translocates protons.

ATP6V1D.fn: Subunit of the V1 complex of vacuolar(H+)-ATPase (V-ATPase), a multisubunit enzyme composed of a peripheral complex (V1) that hydrolyzes ATP and a membrane integral complex (V0) that translocates protons.

ATP6V1E1.fn: Subunit of the V1 complex of vacuolar(H+)-ATPase (V-ATPase), a multisubunit enzyme composed of a peripheral complex (V1) that hydrolyzes ATP and a membrane integral complex (V0) that translocates protons.

ATP6V1F.fn: Subunit of the V1 complex of vacuolar(H+)-ATPase (V-ATPase), a multisubunit enzyme composed of a peripheral complex (V1) that hydrolyzes ATP and a membrane integral complex (V0) that translocates protons.

ATP6V1G1.fn: Subunit of the V1 complex of vacuolar(H+)-ATPase (V-ATPase), a multisubunit enzyme composed of a peripheral complex (V1) that hydrolyzes ATP and a membrane integral complex (V0) that translocates protons.

ATP6V1H.fn: Subunit of the V1 complex of vacuolar(H+)-ATPase (V-ATPase), a multisubunit enzyme composed of a peripheral complex (V1) that hydrolyzes ATP and a membrane integral complex (V0) that translocates protons.

ATR.fn: Serine/threonine protein kinase which activates checkpoint signaling upon genotoxic stresses such as ionizing radiation (IR), ultraviolet light (UV), or DNA replication stalling, thereby acting as a DNA damage sensor.

ATRIP.fn: Required for checkpoint signaling after DNA damage. Required for ATR expression, possibly by stabilizing the protein. .

ATXN10.fn: May play a role in the regulation of cytokinesis. May play a role in signaling by stimulating protein glycosylation. Induces neuritogenesis by activating the Ras-MAP kinase pathway and is necessary for the survival of cerebellar neurons (By similarity).

AURKA.fn: Mitotic serine/threonine kinase that contributes to the regulation of cell cycle progression.

AURKAIP1.protein: Small ribosomal subunit protein bS22, mitochondrial
AURKAIP1.fn: May act as a negative regulator of Aurora-A kinase, by down-regulation through proteasome-dependent degradation.

AURKB.fn: Serine/threonine-protein kinase component of the chromosomal passenger complex (CPC), a complex that acts as a key regulator of mitosis.

BAG6.fn: ATP-independent molecular chaperone preventing the aggregation of misfolded and hydrophobic patches-containing proteins.

BANF1.fn: Non-specific DNA-binding protein that plays key roles in mitotic nuclear reassembly, chromatin organization, DNA damage response, gene expression and intrinsic immunity against foreign DNA.

BANP.fn: Controls V(D)J recombination during T-cell development by repressing T-cell receptor (TCR) beta enhancer function (By similarity).

BAP1.fn: Deubiquitinating enzyme that plays a key role in chromatin by mediating deubiquitination of histone H2A and HCFC1.

BAX.fn: Plays a role in the mitochondrial apoptotic process.

BCAR1.fn: Docking protein which plays a central coordinating role for tyrosine kinase-based signaling related to cell adhesion. Implicated in induction of cell migration and cell branching. Involved in the BCAR3-mediated inhibition of TGFB signaling (By similarity). .

BCAS2.fn: Required for pre-mRNA splicing as component of the activated spliceosome. Component of the PRP19-CDC5L complex that forms an integral part of the spliceosome and is required for activating pre-mRNA splicing.

BCL2L1.fn: Potent inhibitor of cell death. Inhibits activation of caspases. Appears to regulate cell death by blocking the voltage-dependent anion channel (VDAC) by binding to it and preventing the release of the caspase activator, CYC1, from the mitochondrial membrane.

BCLAF1.fn: Death-promoting transcriptional repressor. May be involved in cyclin-D1/CCND1 mRNA stability through the SNARP complex which associates with both the 3'end of the CCND1 gene and its mRNA. .

BCR.fn: Protein with a unique structure having two opposing regulatory activities toward small GTP-binding proteins. The C-terminus is a GTPase-activating protein (GAP) domain which stimulates GTP hydrolysis by RAC1, RAC2 and CDC42.

BCS1L.fn: Chaperone necessary for the incorporation of Rieske iron-sulfur protein UQCRFS1 into the mitochondrial respiratory chain complex III.

BDP1.protein: Transcription factor TFIIIB component B'' homolog
BDP1.fn: General activator of RNA polymerase III transcription. Requires for transcription from all three types of polymerase III promoters. Requires for transcription of genes with internal promoter elements and with promoter elements upstream of the initiation site.

BET1.fn: Required for vesicular transport from the ER to the Golgi complex. Functions as a SNARE involved in the docking process of ER-derived vesicles with the cis-Golgi membrane (By similarity). .

BGLAP.fn: The carboxylated form is one of the main organic components of the bone matrix, which constitutes 1-2% of the total bone protein.

BIRC5.fn: Multitasking protein that has dual roles in promoting cell proliferation and preventing apoptosis. Component of a chromosome passage protein complex (CPC) which is essential for chromosome alignment and segregation during mitosis and cytokinesis.

BMP2K.fn: May be involved in osteoblast differentiation. .

BMS1.fn: GTPase required for the synthesis of 40S ribosomal subunits and for processing of pre-ribosomal RNA (pre-rRNA) at sites A0, A1, and A2.

BNIP1.fn: As part of a SNARE complex may be involved in endoplasmic reticulum membranes fusion and be required for the maintenance of endoplasmic reticulum organization. Also plays a role in apoptosis.

BOD1L1.protein: Biorientation of chromosomes in cell division protein 1-like 1
BOD1L1.fn: Component of the fork protection machinery required to protect stalled/damaged replication forks from uncontrolled DNA2-dependent resection.

BOP1.fn: Component of the PeBoW complex, which is required for maturation of 28S and 5.8S ribosomal RNAs and formation of the 60S ribosome. .

BORA.fn: Required for the activation of AURKA at the onset of mitosis. .

BPTF.fn: Regulatory subunit of the ATP-dependent NURF-1 and NURF-5 ISWI chromatin remodeling complexes, which form ordered nucleosome arrays on chromatin and facilitate access to DNA during DNA-templated processes such as DNA replication, transcription, and repair.

BRAF.fn: Protein kinase involved in the transduction of mitogenic signals from the cell membrane to the nucleus (Probable). Phosphorylates MAP2K1, and thereby activates the MAP kinase signal transduction pathway. Phosphorylates PFKFB2.

BRCA1.fn: E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase that specifically mediates the formation of 'Lys-6'-linked polyubiquitin chains and plays a central role in DNA repair by facilitating cellular responses to DNA damage.

BRCA2.fn: Tumor suppressor protein that maintains genome stability primarily by repairing damaged DNA through homologous recombination (HR).

BRD2.fn: Chromatin reader protein that specifically recognizes and binds histone H4 acetylated at 'Lys-5' and 'Lys-12' (H4K5ac and H4K12ac, respectively), thereby controlling gene expression and remodeling chromatin structures.

BRD4.fn: Chromatin reader protein that recognizes and binds acetylated histones and plays a key role in transmission of epigenetic memory across cell divisions and transcription regulation.

BRD8.fn: May act as a coactivator during transcriptional activation by hormone-activated nuclear receptors (NR). Isoform 2 stimulates transcriptional activation by AR/DHTR, ESR1/NR3A1, RXRA/NR2B1 and THRB/ERBA2.

BRF1.fn: General activator of RNA polymerase which utilizes different TFIIIB complexes at structurally distinct promoters. The isoform 1 is involved in the transcription of tRNA, adenovirus VA1, 7SL and 5S RNA.

BRF2.fn: General activator of RNA polymerase III transcription. Factor exclusively required for RNA polymerase III transcription of genes with promoter elements upstream of the initiation sites.

BRIP1.fn: DNA-dependent ATPase and 5'-3' DNA helicase required for the maintenance of chromosomal stability. Acts late in the Fanconi anemia pathway, after FANCD2 ubiquitination.

BRIX1.fn: Required for biogenesis of the 60S ribosomal subunit.

BRK1.fn: Involved in regulation of actin and microtubule organization. Part of a WAVE complex that activates the Arp2/3 complex. As component of the WAVE1 complex, required for BDNF-NTRK2 endocytic trafficking and signaling from early endosomes (By similarity). .

BTAF1.fn: Regulates transcription in association with TATA binding protein (TBP). Removes TBP from the TATA box in an ATP-dependent manner.

BTF3.fn: When associated with NACA, prevents inappropriate targeting of non-secretory polypeptides to the endoplasmic reticulum (ER).

BUB1.fn: Serine/threonine-protein kinase that performs 2 crucial functions during mitosis: it is essential for spindle-assembly checkpoint signaling and for correct chromosome alignment.

BUB1B.protein: Mitotic checkpoint serine/threonine-protein kinase BUB1 beta
BUB1B.fn: Kinase which is a component of the mitotic checkpoint complex (MCC), which inhibits APC/C and delays chromosome segregation until all chromosomes are properly attached to the mitotic spindle.

BUB3.fn: Has a dual function in spindle-assembly checkpoint signaling and in promoting the establishment of correct kinetochore-microtubule (K-MT) attachments. Promotes the formation of stable end-on bipolar attachments. Necessary for kinetochore localization of BUB1.

BUD13.fn: Involved in pre-mRNA splicing as component of the activated spliceosome. As a component of the minor spliceosome, involved in the splicing of U12-type introns in pre-mRNAs. .

BUD23.fn: S-adenosyl-L-methionine-dependent methyltransferase that specifically methylates the N(7) position of a guanine in 18S rRNA. Requires the methyltransferase adapter protein TRM112 for full rRNA methyltransferase activity.

BUD31.fn: Involved in the pre-mRNA splicing process. May play a role as regulator of AR transcriptional activity; may increase AR transcriptional activity. .

BYSL.fn: Required for processing of 20S pre-rRNA precursor and biogenesis of 40S ribosomal subunits. May be required for trophinin-dependent regulation of cell adhesion during implantation of human embryos. .

C19orf53.protein: Leydig cell tumor 10 kDa protein homolog
C19orf53.fn: May have a potential role in hypercalcemia of malignancy. .

C1D.fn: Plays a role in the recruitment of the RNA exosome complex to pre-rRNA to mediate the 3'-5' end processing of the 5.8S rRNA; this function may include MPHOSPH6.

C1QBP.protein: Complement component 1 Q subcomponent-binding protein, mitochondrial
C1QBP.fn: Multifunctional and multicompartmental protein involved in inflammation and infection processes, ribosome biogenesis, protein synthesis in mitochondria, regulation of apoptosis, transcriptional regulation and pre-mRNA splicing.

C1QTNF4.protein: Complement C1q tumor necrosis factor-related protein 4
C1QTNF4.fn: May be involved in the regulation of the inflammatory network. Its role as pro- or anti-inflammatory seems to be context dependent. Seems to have some role in regulating food intake and energy balance when administered in the brain.

C9orf78.fn: Plays a role in pre-mRNA splicing by promoting usage of the upstream 3'-splice site at alternative NAGNAG splice sites; these are sites featuring alternative acceptor motifs separated by only a few nucleotides. May also modulate exon inclusion events.

CA5A.fn: Mitochondrial carbonic anhydrase that catalyzes the reversible conversion of carbon dioxide to bicarbonate/HCO3.

CABIN1.fn: May be required for replication-independent chromatin assembly. May serve as a negative regulator of T-cell receptor (TCR) signaling via inhibition of calcineurin. Inhibition of activated calcineurin is dependent on both PKC and calcium signals.

CACNB3.protein: Voltage-dependent L-type calcium channel subunit beta-3
CACNB3.fn: Regulatory subunit of the voltage-gated calcium channel that gives rise to L-type calcium currents. Increases CACNA1B peak calcium current and shifts the voltage dependencies of channel activation and inactivation (By similarity).

CACTIN.fn: Plays a role in pre-mRNA splicing by facilitating excision of a subset of introns. Required for the splicing of CDCA5/Sororin, a regulator of sister chromatid cohesion. Involved in the regulation of innate immune response.

CAD.fn: Multifunctional protein that encodes the first 3 enzymatic activities of the de novo pyrimidine pathway: carbamoylphosphate synthetase (CPSase; EC 6.3.5.5), aspartate transcarbamylase (ATCase; EC 2.1.3.2) and dihydroorotase (DHOase; EC 3.5.2.3).

CADM4.fn: Cell adhesion molecule, exhibiting calcium- and magnesium-independent cell-cell adhesion activity.

CALR.fn: Calcium-binding chaperone that promotes folding, oligomeric assembly and quality control in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) via the calreticulin/calnexin cycle.

CAMLG.protein: Guided entry of tail-anchored proteins factor CAMLG
CAMLG.fn: Required for the post-translational delivery of tail-anchored (TA) proteins to the endoplasmic reticulum.

CAP1.fn: Directly regulates filament dynamics and has been implicated in a number of complex developmental and morphological processes, including mRNA localization and the establishment of cell polarity.

CAPZB.fn: F-actin-capping proteins bind in a Ca(2+)-independent manner to the fast growing ends of actin filaments (barbed end) thereby blocking the exchange of subunits at these ends.

CARF.fn: Acts as a transcriptional activator that mediates the calcium- and neuron-selective induction of BDNF exon III transcription. Binds to the consensus calcium-response element CaRE1 5'-CTATTTCGAG-3' sequence. .

CASC3.fn: Required for pre-mRNA splicing as component of the spliceosome. Core component of the splicing-dependent multiprotein exon junction complex (EJC) deposited at splice junctions on mRNAs.

CASP3.fn: Thiol protease that acts as a major effector caspase involved in the execution phase of apoptosis. Following cleavage and activation by initiator caspases (CASP8, CASP9 and/or CASP10), mediates execution of apoptosis by catalyzing cleavage of many proteins.

CASP8AP2.fn: Participates in TNF-induced blockade of glucocorticoid receptor (GR) transactivation at the nuclear receptor coactivator level, upstream and independently of NF-kappa-B. Suppresses both NCOA2- and NCOA3-induced enhancement of GR transactivation.

CAST.fn: Specific inhibition of calpain (calcium-dependent cysteine protease). Plays a key role in postmortem tenderization of meat and have been proposed to be involved in muscle protein degradation in living tissue.

CBFA2T3.fn: Transcriptional corepressor which facilitates transcriptional repression via its association with DNA-binding transcription factors and recruitment of other corepressors and histone-modifying enzymes.

CBLL1.fn: E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase that mediates ubiquitination of several tyrosine-phosphorylated Src substrates, including CDH1, CTTN and DOK1 (By similarity). Targets CDH1 for endocytosis and degradation (By similarity).

CBLN1.fn: Required for synapse integrity and synaptic plasticity.

CBX1.fn: Component of heterochromatin, which recognizes and binds histone H3 tails methylated at 'Lys-9', leading to epigenetic repression. Also recognizes and binds histone H1.4 methylated at 'Lys-26' (H1.4K26me).

CCAR1.protein: Cell division cycle and apoptosis regulator protein 1
CCAR1.fn: Associates with components of the Mediator and p160 coactivator complexes that play a role as intermediaries transducing regulatory signals from upstream transcriptional activator proteins to basal transcription machinery at the core promoter.

CCDC144A.fn: May play a role in preventing the formation of kidney stones through inhibition of calcium oxalate monohydrate (COM) crystallization, attenuating COM-induced apoptotic injury to renal epithelial cells.

CCDC59.fn: Component of the transcription complexes of the pulmonary surfactant-associated protein-B (SFTPB) and -C (SFTPC). Enhances homeobox protein Nkx-2.1-activated SFTPB and SFTPC promoter activities. .

CCDC6.fn: Acts as a structural scaffold that organizes free PP2Ac into a configuration that FBXO42 can recognize and ubiquitinate, leading to its proteasomal degradation.

CCDC78.fn: Component of the deuterosome, a structure that promotes de novo centriole amplification in multiciliated cells that can generate more than 100 centrioles.

CCDC86.fn: Required for proper chromosome segregation during mitosis and error-free mitotic progression. .

CCNA2.fn: Essential for the control of the cell cycle at G1/S and G2/M transition. Functions through the formation of specific serine/threonine protein kinase holoenzyme complexes with the cyclin-dependent protein kinases CDK1 or CDK2.

CCNB1.fn: Essential for the control of the cell cycle at the G2/M (mitosis) transition. Binds and activates cyclin-dependent protein kinase CDK1/CDC2. .

CCNC.fn: Component of the Mediator complex, a coactivator involved in regulated gene transcription of nearly all RNA polymerase II-dependent genes.

CCND1.fn: Regulatory component of the cyclin D1-CDK4 (DC) complex that phosphorylates and inhibits members of the retinoblastoma (RB) protein family including RB1 and regulates the cell-cycle during G(1)/S transition.

CCND3.fn: Regulatory component of the cyclin D3-CDK4 (DC) complex that phosphorylates and inhibits members of the retinoblastoma (RB) protein family including RB1 and regulates the cell-cycle during G(1)/S transition.

CCNH.fn: Component of the CDK-activating kinase (CAK) complex, a master regulator of CDK activity by catalyzing the activating threonine phosphorylation of CDKs. Binds and activates cyclin-dependent protein kinase CDK7, the catalytic subunit of CAK.

CCNK.fn: Regulatory subunit of cyclin-dependent kinases that mediates activation of target kinases.

CCNL1.fn: Regulatory component of the cyclin-L-CDK11 complex that regulates transcription and pre-mRNA splicing. Inhibited by the CDK-specific inhibitor CDKN1A/p21. May be a candidate proto-oncogene in head and neck squamous cell carcinomas (HNSCC). .

CCNQ.fn: Activating cyclin for the cyclin-associated kinase CDK10. .

CCP110.fn: Necessary for centrosome duplication at different stages of procentriole formation. Acts as a key negative regulator of ciliogenesis in collaboration with CEP97 by capping the mother centriole thereby preventing cilia formation.

CCT2.fn: Component of the chaperonin-containing T-complex (TRiC), a molecular chaperone complex that assists the folding of actin, tubulin and other proteins upon ATP hydrolysis.

CCT3.fn: Component of the chaperonin-containing T-complex (TRiC), a molecular chaperone complex that assists the folding of actin, tubulin and other proteins upon ATP hydrolysis.

CCT4.fn: Component of the chaperonin-containing T-complex (TRiC), a molecular chaperone complex that assists the folding of actin, tubulin and other proteins upon ATP hydrolysis.

CCT5.fn: Component of the chaperonin-containing T-complex (TRiC), a molecular chaperone complex that assists the folding of actin, tubulin and other proteins upon ATP hydrolysis.

CCT6A.fn: Component of the chaperonin-containing T-complex (TRiC), a molecular chaperone complex that assists the folding of actin, tubulin and other proteins upon ATP hydrolysis.

CCT7.fn: Component of the chaperonin-containing T-complex (TRiC), a molecular chaperone complex that assists the folding of actin, tubulin and other proteins upon ATP hydrolysis.

CCT8.fn: Component of the chaperonin-containing T-complex (TRiC), a molecular chaperone complex that assists the folding of actin, tubulin and other proteins upon ATP hydrolysis.

CD2BP2.fn: Involved in pre-mRNA splicing as component of the U5 snRNP complex that is involved in spliceosome assembly. .

CD8B.protein: T-cell surface glycoprotein CD8 beta chain
CD8B.fn: Integral membrane glycoprotein that plays an essential role in the immune response and serves multiple functions in responses against both external and internal offenses. In T-cells, functions primarily as a coreceptor for MHC class I molecule:peptide complex.

CDAN1.fn: May act as a negative regulator of ASF1 in chromatin assembly. .

CDC123.protein: Translation initiation factor eIF2 assembly protein
CDC123.fn: ATP-dependent protein-folding chaperone for the eIF2 complex. Binds to the gamma subunit of the eIF2 complex which allows the subunit to assemble with the alpha and beta subunits (By similarity). .

CDC16.fn: Component of the anaphase promoting complex/cyclosome (APC/C), a cell cycle-regulated E3 ubiquitin ligase that controls progression through the cell cycle.

CDC20.fn: Substrate-specific adapter and activator of the anaphase promoting complex/cyclosome (APC/C) that confers substrate specificity by binding to substrates and targeting them to the APC/C for ubiquitination and degradation.

CDC23.fn: Component of the anaphase promoting complex/cyclosome (APC/C), a cell cycle-regulated E3 ubiquitin ligase that controls progression through the cell cycle.

CDC26.fn: Component of the anaphase promoting complex/cyclosome (APC/C), a cell cycle-regulated E3 ubiquitin ligase that controls progression through the cell cycle.

CDC27.fn: Component of the anaphase promoting complex/cyclosome (APC/C), a cell cycle-regulated E3 ubiquitin ligase that controls progression through the cell cycle.

CDC37.fn: Co-chaperone that binds to numerous kinases and promotes their interaction with the Hsp90 complex, resulting in stabilization and promotion of their activity. Inhibits HSP90AA1 ATPase activity. .

CDC40.fn: Required for pre-mRNA splicing as component of the activated spliceosome. Plays an important role in embryonic brain development; this function does not require proline isomerization. .

CDC42.fn: Plasma membrane-associated small GTPase which cycles between an active GTP-bound and an inactive GDP-bound state. In active state binds to a variety of effector proteins to regulate cellular responses. Involved in epithelial cell polarization processes.

CDC45.fn: Required for initiation of chromosomal DNA replication. Core component of CDC45-MCM-GINS (CMG) helicase, the molecular machine that unwinds template DNA during replication, and around which the replisome is built. .

CDC5L.fn: DNA-binding protein involved in cell cycle control. May act as a transcription activator. Plays a role in pre-mRNA splicing as core component of precatalytic, catalytic and postcatalytic spliceosomal complexes.

CDC6.fn: Involved in the initiation of DNA replication. Also participates in checkpoint controls that ensure DNA replication is completed before mitosis is initiated.

CDC7.fn: Kinase involved in initiation of DNA replication. Phosphorylates critical substrates that regulate the G1/S phase transition and initiation of DNA replication, such as MCM proteins and CLASPIN. .

CDC73.fn: Tumor suppressor probably involved in transcriptional and post-transcriptional control pathways. May be involved in cell cycle progression through the regulation of cyclin D1/PRAD1 expression.

CDCA5.fn: Regulator of sister chromatid cohesion in mitosis, stabilizing cohesin complex association with chromatin. May antagonize the action of WAPL which stimulates cohesin dissociation from chromatin.

CDCA8.fn: Component of the chromosomal passenger complex (CPC), a complex that acts as a key regulator of mitosis.

CDIPT.fn: Catalyzes the biosynthesis of phosphatidylinositol (PtdIns) as well as PtdIns:inositol exchange reaction. May thus act to reduce an excessive cellular PtdIns content.

CDK1.fn: Plays a key role in the control of the eukaryotic cell cycle by modulating the centrosome cycle as well as mitotic onset; promotes G2-M transition via association with multiple interphase cyclins.

CDK11A.fn: Cyclin-dependent protein kinase that acts as a regulator of transcription and pre-mRNA splicing.

CDK12.fn: Cyclin-dependent kinase that phosphorylates the C-terminal domain (CTD) of the large subunit of RNA polymerase II (POLR2A), thereby acting as a key regulator of transcription elongation.

CDK2.fn: Serine/threonine-protein kinase involved in the control of the cell cycle; essential for meiosis, but dispensable for mitosis. Phosphorylates CABLES1, CTNNB1, CDK2AP2, ERCC6, NBN, USP37, p53/TP53, NPM1, CDK7, RB1, BRCA2, MYC, NPAT, SUV39H1, EZH2.

CDK4.fn: Ser/Thr-kinase component of cyclin D-CDK4 (DC) complexes that phosphorylate and inhibit members of the retinoblastoma (RB) protein family including RB1 and regulate the cell-cycle during G(1)/S transition.

CDK6.fn: Serine/threonine-protein kinase involved in the control of the cell cycle and differentiation; promotes G1/S transition. Phosphorylates pRB/RB1 and NPM1.

CDK7.fn: Serine/threonine kinase involved in cell cycle control and in RNA polymerase II-mediated RNA transcription. As a cyclin-dependent kinase, CDK7 is activated by the binding to cyclin-H/CCNH and the CDK-activating kinase assembly factor MAT1.

CDK9.fn: Protein kinase involved in the regulation of transcription.

CDKN1A.fn: Plays an important role in controlling cell cycle progression and DNA damage-induced G2 arrest. Involved in p53/TP53 mediated inhibition of cellular proliferation in response to DNA damage.

CDT1.fn: Required for both DNA replication and mitosis. DNA replication licensing factor, required for pre-replication complex assembly.

CEBPG.fn: Transcription factor that binds to the promoter and the enhancer regions of target genes. Binds to the enhancer element PRE-I (positive regulatory element-I) of the IL-4 gene. Binds to the promoter and the enhancer of the immunoglobulin heavy chain.

CEBPZ.fn: Stimulates transcription from the HSP70 promoter.

CENPA.fn: Histone H3-like nucleosomal protein that is specifically found in centromeric nucleosomes. Replaces conventional H3 in the nucleosome core of centromeric chromatin that serves as an assembly site for the inner kinetochore.

CENPC.fn: Component of the CENPA-NAC (nucleosome-associated) complex, a complex that plays a central role in assembly of kinetochore proteins, mitotic progression and chromosome segregation.

CENPE.fn: Microtubule plus-end-directed kinetochore motor which plays an important role in chromosome congression, microtubule-kinetochore conjugation and spindle assembly checkpoint activation.

CENPH.fn: Component of the CENPA-NAC (nucleosome-associated) complex, a complex that plays a central role in assembly of kinetochore proteins, mitotic progression and chromosome segregation.

CENPI.fn: Component of the CENPA-CAD (nucleosome distal) complex, a complex recruited to centromeres which is involved in assembly of kinetochore proteins, mitotic progression and chromosome segregation.

CENPK.fn: Component of the CENPA-CAD (nucleosome distal) complex, a complex recruited to centromeres which is involved in assembly of kinetochore proteins, mitotic progression and chromosome segregation.

CENPN.fn: Component of the CENPA-NAC (nucleosome-associated) complex, a complex that plays a central role in assembly of kinetochore proteins, mitotic progression and chromosome segregation.

CENPP.fn: Component of the CENPA-CAD (nucleosome distal) complex, a complex recruited to centromeres which is involved in assembly of kinetochore proteins, mitotic progression and chromosome segregation.

CENPT.fn: Component of the CENPA-NAC (nucleosome-associated) complex, a complex that plays a central role in assembly of kinetochore proteins, mitotic progression and chromosome segregation.

CENPW.fn: Component of the CENPA-NAC (nucleosome-associated) complex, a complex that plays a central role in assembly of kinetochore proteins, mitotic progression and chromosome segregation (By similarity).

CEP152.fn: Necessary for centrosome duplication; the function also seems to involve CEP63, CDK5RAP2 and WDR62 through a stepwise assembled complex at the centrosome that recruits CDK2 required for centriole duplication.

CEP192.fn: Required for mitotic centrosome maturation and bipolar spindle assembly. Appears to be a major regulator of pericentriolar material (PCM) recruitment, centrosome maturation, and centriole duplication. Centrosome-specific activating scaffold for AURKA and PLK1.

CEP68.fn: Involved in maintenance of centrosome cohesion, probably as part of a linker structure which prevents centrosome splitting. Required for localization of CDK5RAP2 to the centrosome during interphase. Contributes to CROCC/rootletin filament formation. .

CEP85.fn: Acts as a regulator of centriole duplication through a direct interaction with STIL, a key factor involved in the early steps of centriole formation.

CEP97.fn: Acts as a key negative regulator of ciliogenesis in collaboration with CCP110 by capping the mother centriole thereby preventing cilia formation. Required for recruitment of CCP110 to the centrosome. .

CFDP1.fn: Required for the structural stability of pericentromeric heterochromatin.

CFL1.fn: Binds to F-actin and exhibits pH-sensitive F-actin depolymerizing activity. In conjunction with the subcortical maternal complex (SCMC), plays an essential role for zygotes to progress beyond the first embryonic cell divisions via regulation of actin dynamics.

CHAF1A.fn: Acts as a component of the histone chaperone complex chromatin assembly factor 1 (CAF-1), which assembles histone octamers onto DNA during replication and repair.

CHAF1B.fn: Acts as a component of the histone chaperone complex chromatin assembly factor 1 (CAF-1), which assembles histone octamers onto DNA during replication and repair.

CHCHD2.fn: Transcription factor. Binds to the oxygen responsive element of COX4I2 and activates its transcription under hypoxia conditions (4% oxygen), as well as normoxia conditions (20% oxygen). .

CHCHD3.fn: Component of the MICOS complex, a large protein complex of the mitochondrial inner membrane that plays crucial roles in the maintenance of crista junctions, inner membrane architecture, and formation of contact sites to the outer membrane.

CHCHD4.protein: Mitochondrial intermembrane space import and assembly protein 40
CHCHD4.fn: Central component of a redox-sensitive mitochondrial intermembrane space import machinery which is required for the biogenesis of respiratory chain complexes.

CHD4.fn: ATP-dependent chromatin-remodeling factor that binds and distorts nucleosomal DNA. Acts as a component of the histone deacetylase NuRD complex which participates in the remodeling of chromatin.

CHEK1.fn: Serine/threonine-protein kinase which is required for checkpoint-mediated cell cycle arrest and activation of DNA repair in response to the presence of DNA damage or unreplicated DNA.

CHERP.fn: Involved in calcium homeostasis, growth and proliferation. .

CHMP1A.fn: Probable peripherally associated component of the endosomal sorting required for transport complex III (ESCRT-III) which is involved in multivesicular bodies (MVBs) formation and sorting of endosomal cargo proteins into MVBs.

CHMP2A.fn: Probable core component of the endosomal sorting required for transport complex III (ESCRT-III) which is involved in multivesicular bodies (MVBs) formation and sorting of endosomal cargo proteins into MVBs.

CHMP3.fn: Probable core component of the endosomal sorting required for transport complex III (ESCRT-III) which is involved in multivesicular bodies (MVBs) formation and sorting of endosomal cargo proteins into MVBs.

CHMP4B.fn: Probable core component of the endosomal sorting required for transport complex III (ESCRT-III) which is involved in multivesicular bodies (MVBs) formation and sorting of endosomal cargo proteins into MVBs.

CHMP5.fn: Probable peripherally associated component of the endosomal sorting required for transport complex III (ESCRT-III) which is involved in multivesicular bodies (MVBs) formation and sorting of endosomal cargo proteins into MVBs.

CHMP6.fn: Probable core component of the endosomal sorting required for transport complex III (ESCRT-III) which is involved in multivesicular bodies (MVBs) formation and sorting of endosomal cargo proteins into MVBs.

CHMP7.fn: ESCRT-III-like protein required to recruit the ESCRT-III complex to the nuclear envelope (NE) during late anaphase. Together with SPAST, the ESCRT-III complex promotes NE sealing and mitotic spindle disassembly during late anaphase.

CHORDC1.fn: Regulates centrosome duplication, probably by inhibiting the kinase activity of ROCK2. Proposed to act as co-chaperone for HSP90. May play a role in the regulation of NOD1 via a HSP90 chaperone complex. In vitro, has intrinsic chaperone activity.

CHTF18.fn: Chromosome cohesion factor involved in sister chromatid cohesion and fidelity of chromosome transmission.

CHTF8.fn: Chromosome cohesion factor involved in sister chromatid cohesion and fidelity of chromosome transmission.

CHTOP.fn: Plays an important role in the ligand-dependent activation of estrogen receptor target genes. May play a role in the silencing of fetal globin genes.

CIAO1.protein: Probable cytosolic iron-sulfur protein assembly protein CIAO1
CIAO1.fn: Key component of the cytosolic iron-sulfur protein assembly (CIA) complex, a multiprotein complex that mediates the incorporation of iron-sulfur cluster into extramitochondrial Fe/S proteins.

CIAPIN1.fn: Component of the cytosolic iron-sulfur (Fe-S) protein assembly (CIA) machinery required for the maturation of extramitochondrial Fe-S proteins.

CINP.fn: Component of the DNA replication complex, which interacts with two kinases, CDK2 and CDC7, thereby providing a functional and physical link between CDK2 and CDC7 during firing of the origins of replication.

CKAP5.fn: Binds to the plus end of microtubules and regulates microtubule dynamics and microtubule organization. Acts as a processive microtubule polymerase. Promotes cytoplasmic microtubule nucleation and elongation. Plays a major role in organizing spindle poles.

CLASRP.fn: Probably functions as an alternative splicing regulator. May regulate the mRNA splicing of genes such as CLK1. May act by regulating members of the CLK kinase family (By similarity). .

CLCC1.fn: Anion-selective channel with Ca(2+)-dependent and voltage-independent gating. Permeable to small monovalent anions with selectivity for bromide > chloride > nitrate > fluoride (By similarity).

CLK2.fn: Dual specificity kinase acting on both serine/threonine and tyrosine-containing substrates. Phosphorylates serine- and arginine-rich (SR) proteins of the spliceosomal complex.

CLNS1A.fn: Involved in both the assembly of spliceosomal snRNPs and the methylation of Sm proteins.

CLOCK.protein: Circadian locomoter output cycles protein kaput
CLOCK.fn: Transcriptional activator which forms a core component of the circadian clock.

CLP1.fn: Polynucleotide kinase that can phosphorylate the 5'-hydroxyl groups of double-stranded RNA (dsRNA), single-stranded RNA (ssRNA), double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) and double-stranded DNA:RNA hybrids.

CLPB.fn: Functions as a regulatory ATPase and participates in secretion/protein trafficking process. Has ATP-dependent protein disaggregase activity and is required to maintain the solubility of key mitochondrial proteins.

CLSPN.fn: Required for checkpoint mediated cell cycle arrest in response to inhibition of DNA replication or to DNA damage induced by both ionizing and UV irradiation.

CLTC.fn: Clathrin is the major protein of the polyhedral coat of coated pits and vesicles. Two different adapter protein complexes link the clathrin lattice either to the plasma membrane or to the trans-Golgi network.

CMPK1.fn: Catalyzes the phosphorylation of pyrimidine nucleoside monophosphates at the expense of ATP. Plays an important role in de novo pyrimidine nucleotide biosynthesis. Has preference for UMP and CMP as phosphate acceptors.

CMTR1.fn: S-adenosyl-L-methionine-dependent methyltransferase that mediates mRNA cap1 2'-O-ribose methylation to the 5'-cap structure of mRNAs.

CMTR2.fn: S-adenosyl-L-methionine-dependent methyltransferase that mediates mRNA cap2 2'-O-ribose methylation to the 5'-cap structure of mRNAs.

CNIH4.fn: Involved in G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) trafficking from the endoplasmic reticulum to the cell surface; it promotes the exit of GPCRs from the early secretory pathway, likely through interaction with the COPII machinery. .

CNN2.fn: Thin filament-associated protein that is implicated in the regulation and modulation of smooth muscle contraction. It is capable of binding to actin, calmodulin and tropomyosin. The interaction of calponin with actin inhibits the actomyosin Mg-ATPase activity.

CNOT1.fn: Scaffolding component of the CCR4-NOT complex which is one of the major cellular mRNA deadenylases and is linked to various cellular processes including bulk mRNA degradation, miRNA-mediated repression, translational repression during translational initiation

CNOT10.fn: Component of the CCR4-NOT complex which is one of the major cellular mRNA deadenylases and is linked to various cellular processes including bulk mRNA degradation, miRNA-mediated repression, translational repression during translational initiation and general

CNOT11.fn: Component of the CCR4-NOT complex which is one of the major cellular mRNA deadenylases and is linked to various cellular processes including bulk mRNA degradation, miRNA-mediated repression, translational repression during translational initiation and general

CNOT2.fn: Component of the CCR4-NOT complex which is one of the major cellular mRNA deadenylases and is linked to various cellular processes including bulk mRNA degradation, miRNA-mediated repression, translational repression during translational initiation and general

CNOT3.fn: Component of the CCR4-NOT complex which is one of the major cellular mRNA deadenylases and is linked to various cellular processes including bulk mRNA degradation, miRNA-mediated repression, translational repression during translational initiation and general

CNOT9.fn: Component of the CCR4-NOT complex which is one of the major cellular mRNA deadenylases and is linked to various cellular processes including bulk mRNA degradation, miRNA-mediated repression, translational repression during translational initiation and general

COA5.fn: Assembly factor for cytochrome c oxidase (respiratory chain complex IV). Stabilizes an early formation of cytochrome c oxidase assembly factors, until it is displaced by the metallochaperone copper-delivery protein COX17. .

COASY.fn: Bifunctional enzyme that catalyzes the fourth step of the coenzyme A biosynthetic pathway, the adenylation of 4'-phosphopantetheine, and the fifth step, the phosphorylation of dephospho-CoA to CoA. .

COG2.fn: Required for normal Golgi morphology and function.

COG3.fn: Involved in ER-Golgi transport. Also involved in retrograde (Golgi to ER) transport. .

COG4.fn: Required for normal Golgi function. Plays a role in SNARE-pin assembly and Golgi-to-ER retrograde transport via its interaction with SCFD1. .

COPA.fn: The coatomer is a cytosolic protein complex that binds to dilysine motifs and reversibly associates with Golgi non-clathrin-coated vesicles, which further mediate biosynthetic protein transport from the ER, via the Golgi up to the trans Golgi network.

COPB1.fn: The coatomer is a cytosolic protein complex that binds to dilysine motifs and reversibly associates with Golgi non-clathrin-coated vesicles, which further mediate biosynthetic protein transport from the ER, via the Golgi up to the trans Golgi network.

COPB2.fn: The coatomer is a cytosolic protein complex that binds to dilysine motifs and reversibly associates with Golgi non-clathrin-coated vesicles, which further mediate biosynthetic protein transport from the ER, via the Golgi up to the trans Golgi network.

COPE.fn: The coatomer is a cytosolic protein complex that binds to dilysine motifs and reversibly associates with Golgi non-clathrin-coated vesicles, which further mediate biosynthetic protein transport from the ER, via the Golgi up to the trans Golgi network.

COPG1.fn: The coatomer is a cytosolic protein complex that binds to dilysine motifs and reversibly associates with Golgi non-clathrin-coated vesicles, which further mediate biosynthetic protein transport from the ER, via the Golgi up to the trans Golgi network.

COPS2.fn: Component of the COP9 signalosome (CSN), a master regulator of the ubiquitin conjugation pathway. CSN mediates the deneddylation of the cullin subunits of all cullin-RING ligases.

COPS3.fn: Component of the COP9 signalosome (CSN), a master regulator of the ubiquitin conjugation pathway. CSN mediates the deneddylation of the cullin subunits of all cullin-RING ligases.

COPS4.fn: Component of the COP9 signalosome (CSN), a master regulator of the ubiquitin conjugation pathway. CSN mediates the deneddylation of the cullin subunits of all cullin-RING ligases.

COPS5.fn: Metalloprotease and the catalytic component of the COP9 signalosome (CSN), a master regulator of the ubiquitin conjugation pathway. CSN mediates the deneddylation of the cullin subunits of all cullin-RING ligases.

COPS6.fn: Component of the COP9 signalosome (CSN), a master regulator of the ubiquitin conjugation pathway. CSN mediates the deneddylation of the cullin subunits of all cullin-RING ligases.

COPS8.fn: Component of the COP9 signalosome (CSN), a master regulator of the ubiquitin conjugation pathway. CSN mediates the deneddylation of the cullin subunits of all cullin-RING ligases.

COPZ1.fn: Component of the coatomer complex, involved in retrograde Golgi-to-ER transport.

COQ2.fn: Mediates the second step in the final reaction sequence of coenzyme Q (CoQ) biosynthesis. Catalyzes the prenylation of para-hydroxybenzoate (PHB) with an all-trans polyprenyl donor (such as all-trans-decaprenyl diphosphate).

COQ4.protein: Ubiquinone biosynthesis protein COQ4 homolog, mitochondrial
COQ4.fn: Lyase that catalyzes the C1-decarboxylation of 4-hydroxy-3-methoxy-5-(all-trans-decaprenyl)benzoic acid into 2-methoxy-6-(all-trans-decaprenyl)phenol during ubiquinone biosynthesis. .

COQ5.fn: Methyltransferase required for the conversion of 2-decaprenyl-6-methoxy-1,4-benzoquinol (DDMQH2) to 2-decaprenyl-3-methyl-6-methoxy-1,4-benzoquinol (DMQH2). .

COTL1.fn: Binds to F-actin in a calcium-independent manner. Has no direct effect on actin depolymerization. Acts as a chaperone for ALOX5 (5LO), influencing both its stability and activity in leukotrienes synthesis. .

COX10.fn: Converts protoheme IX and farnesyl diphosphate to heme O. .

COX11.protein: Cytochrome c oxidase assembly protein COX11, mitochondrial
COX11.fn: Assembly factor for cytochrome c oxidase (respiratory chain complex IV, CIV). Probably acts as a metallochaperone that delivers copper to the copper B site of COX1. .

COX15.fn: Catalyzes the second reaction in the biosynthesis of heme A, a prosthetic group of mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase (CcO). Heme A is synthesized from heme B by two sequential enzymatic reactions catalyzed by heme O synthase (HOS) and heme A synthase (HAS).

COX17.fn: Copper metallochaperone involved in the assembly of cytochrome c oxidase (respiratory chain complex IV, CIV).

COX5A.fn: Component of the cytochrome c oxidase, the last enzyme in the mitochondrial electron transport chain which drives oxidative phosphorylation.

COX5B.fn: Component of the cytochrome c oxidase, the last enzyme in the mitochondrial electron transport chain which drives oxidative phosphorylation.

COX6C.fn: Component of the cytochrome c oxidase, the last enzyme in the mitochondrial electron transport chain which drives oxidative phosphorylation.

COX7B.fn: Component of the cytochrome c oxidase, the last enzyme in the mitochondrial electron transport chain which drives oxidative phosphorylation.

COX7C.fn: Component of the cytochrome c oxidase, the last enzyme in the mitochondrial electron transport chain which drives oxidative phosphorylation.

CPAMD8.protein: C3 and PZP-like alpha-2-macroglobulin domain-containing protein 8

CPEB1.fn: Sequence-specific RNA-binding protein that regulates mRNA cytoplasmic polyadenylation and translation initiation during oocyte maturation, early development and at postsynapse sites of neurons.

CPNE1.fn: Calcium-dependent phospholipid-binding protein that plays a role in calcium-mediated intracellular processes. Involved in the TNF receptor signaling pathway in a calcium-dependent manner. Exhibits calcium-dependent phospholipid binding properties.

CPNE7.fn: Calcium-dependent phospholipid-binding protein that may play a role in calcium-mediated intracellular processes. .

CPOX.fn: Catalyzes the aerobic oxidative decarboxylation of propionate groups of rings A and B of coproporphyrinogen-III to yield the vinyl groups in protoporphyrinogen-IX and participates to the sixth step in the heme biosynthetic pathway. .

CPSF1.protein: Cleavage and polyadenylation specificity factor subunit 1
CPSF1.fn: Component of the cleavage and polyadenylation specificity factor (CPSF) complex that plays a key role in pre-mRNA 3'-end formation, recognizing the AAUAAA signal sequence and interacting with poly(A) polymerase and other factors to bring about cleavage and pol

CPSF2.protein: Cleavage and polyadenylation specificity factor subunit 2
CPSF2.fn: Component of the cleavage and polyadenylation specificity factor (CPSF) complex that play a key role in pre-mRNA 3'-end formation, recognizing the AAUAAA signal sequence and interacting with poly(A) polymerase and other factors to bring about cleavage and poly

CPSF3.protein: Cleavage and polyadenylation specificity factor subunit 3
CPSF3.fn: Component of the cleavage and polyadenylation specificity factor (CPSF) complex that plays a key role in pre-mRNA 3'-end formation, recognizing the AAUAAA signal sequence and interacting with poly(A) polymerase and other factors to bring about cleavage and pol

CPSF4.protein: Cleavage and polyadenylation specificity factor subunit 4
CPSF4.fn: Component of the cleavage and polyadenylation specificity factor (CPSF) complex that play a key role in pre-mRNA 3'-end formation, recognizing the AAUAAA signal sequence and interacting with poly(A) polymerase and other factors to bring about cleavage and poly

CPSF6.protein: Cleavage and polyadenylation specificity factor subunit 6
CPSF6.fn: Component of the cleavage factor Im (CFIm) complex that functions as an activator of the pre-mRNA 3'-end cleavage and polyadenylation processing required for the maturation of pre-mRNA into functional mRNAs.

CRCP.protein: DNA-directed RNA polymerase III subunit RPC9
CRCP.fn: DNA-dependent RNA polymerase catalyzes the transcription of DNA into RNA using the four ribonucleoside triphosphates as substrates.

CRKL.fn: May mediate the transduction of intracellular signals.

CRLS1.fn: Catalyzes the synthesis of cardiolipin (CL) (diphosphatidylglycerol) by specifically transferring a phosphatidyl group from CDP-diacylglycerol to phosphatidylglycerol (PG).

CRNKL1.fn: Involved in pre-mRNA splicing process. As a component of the minor spliceosome, involved in the splicing of U12-type introns in pre-mRNAs (Probable). .

CS.fn: Key enzyme of the Krebs tricarboxylic acid cycle which catalyzes the synthesis of citrate from acetyl coenzyme A and oxaloacetate. .

CSDE1.fn: RNA-binding protein involved in translationally coupled mRNA turnover.

CSE1L.fn: Export receptor for importin-alpha. Mediates importin-alpha re-export from the nucleus to the cytoplasm after import substrates (cargos) have been released into the nucleoplasm.

CSH2.fn: Produced only during pregnancy and is involved in stimulating lactation, fetal growth and metabolism. Does not interact with GHR but only activates PRLR through zinc-induced dimerization. .

CSNK1A1.fn: Casein kinases are operationally defined by their preferential utilization of acidic proteins such as caseins as substrates. Phosphorylates a large number of proteins. Participates in Wnt signaling. Phosphorylates CTNNB1 at 'Ser-45'.

CSNK2B.fn: Regulatory subunit of casein kinase II/CK2.

CSTF1.fn: One of the multiple factors required for polyadenylation and 3'-end cleavage of mammalian pre-mRNAs. May be responsible for the interaction of CSTF with other factors to form a stable complex on the pre-mRNA. .

CSTF3.fn: One of the multiple factors required for polyadenylation and 3'-end cleavage of mammalian pre-mRNAs.

CTBP2.fn: Corepressor targeting diverse transcription regulators. Functions in brown adipose tissue (BAT) differentiation (By similarity). .; Isoform 2 probably acts as a scaffold for specialized synapses.

CTCF.fn: Chromatin binding factor that binds to DNA sequence specific sites and regulates the 3D structure of chromatin. Binds together strands of DNA, thus forming chromatin loops, and anchors DNA to cellular structures, such as the nuclear lamina.

CTDP1.protein: RNA polymerase II subunit A C-terminal domain phosphatase
CTDP1.fn: Processively dephosphorylates 'Ser-2' and 'Ser-5' of the heptad repeats YSPTSPS in the C-terminal domain of the largest RNA polymerase II subunit. This promotes the activity of RNA polymerase II.

CTNNB1.fn: Key downstream component of the canonical Wnt signaling pathway.

CTNNBL1.fn: Component of the PRP19-CDC5L complex that forms an integral part of the spliceosome and is required for activating pre-mRNA splicing.

CTPS1.fn: Cytidine triphosphate synthase involved in the de novo synthesis of CTP, a precursor of DNA, RNA and phospholipids. Catalyzes the ATP-dependent amination of UTP to CTP with either L-glutamine or ammonia as a source of nitrogen.

CTR9.fn: Component of the PAF1 complex (PAF1C) which has multiple functions during transcription by RNA polymerase II and is implicated in regulation of development and maintenance of embryonic stem cell pluripotency.

CTU2.fn: Plays a central role in 2-thiolation of mcm(5)S(2)U at tRNA wobble positions of tRNA(Lys), tRNA(Glu) and tRNA(Gln). May act by forming a heterodimer with CTU1/ATPBD3 that ligates sulfur from thiocarboxylated URM1 onto the uridine of tRNAs at wobble position. .

CUL1.fn: Core component of multiple cullin-RING-based SCF (SKP1-CUL1-F-box protein) E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase complexes, which mediate the ubiquitination of proteins involved in cell cycle progression, signal transduction and transcription.

CUL2.fn: Core component of multiple cullin-RING-based ECS (ElonginB/C-CUL2/5-SOCS-box protein) E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase complexes, which mediate the ubiquitination of target proteins.

CUL3.fn: Core component of multiple cullin-RING-based BCR (BTB-CUL3-RBX1) E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase complexes which mediate the ubiquitination and subsequent proteasomal degradation of target proteins.

CUL7.fn: Core component of the 3M and Cul7-RING(FBXW8) complexes, which mediate the ubiquitination and subsequent proteasomal degradation of target proteins. Core component of the 3M complex, a complex required to regulate microtubule dynamics and genome integrity.

CWC15.fn: Involved in pre-mRNA splicing as component of the spliceosome. Component of the PRP19-CDC5L complex that forms an integral part of the spliceosome and is required for activating pre-mRNA splicing.

CWC22.fn: Required for pre-mRNA splicing as component of the spliceosome. As a component of the minor spliceosome, involved in the splicing of U12-type introns in pre-mRNAs (Probable). Promotes exon-junction complex (EJC) assembly.

CWC25.fn: Involved in pre-mRNA splicing as component of the spliceosome. .

CWF19L2.fn: RNA-binding protein which regulates alternative splicing (By similarity). Recognizes the 5'-GG[A/C][A/G]G[A/C/G]-3' motif with 58% of target sequences containing a 5'-GGCAGA-3' motif (By similarity).

CXXC1.fn: Transcriptional activator that exhibits a unique DNA binding specificity for CpG unmethylated motifs with a preference for CpGG. .

CYC1.fn: Component of the ubiquinol-cytochrome c oxidoreductase, a multisubunit transmembrane complex that is part of the mitochondrial electron transport chain which drives oxidative phosphorylation.

CYCS.fn: Electron carrier protein. The oxidized form of the cytochrome c heme group can accept an electron from the heme group of the cytochrome c1 subunit of cytochrome reductase.

CYFIP1.fn: Component of the CYFIP1-EIF4E-FMR1 complex which binds to the mRNA cap and mediates translational repression. In the CYFIP1-EIF4E-FMR1 complex this subunit is an adapter between EIF4E and FMR1.

CYP4F11.fn: A cytochrome P450 monooxygenase involved in the metabolism of various endogenous substrates, including fatty acids and their oxygenated derivatives (oxylipins).

CYREN.protein: Cell cycle regulator of non-homologous end joining
CYREN.fn: Cell-cycle-specific regulator of classical non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) of DNA double-strand break (DSB) repair, which can act both as an activator or inhibitor of NHEJ, depending on the cell cycle phase.

DAD1.fn: Subunit of the oligosaccharyl transferase (OST) complex that catalyzes the initial transfer of a defined glycan (Glc(3)Man(9)GlcNAc(2) in eukaryotes) from the lipid carrier dolichol-pyrophosphate to an asparagine residue within an Asn-Xaa-Ser/Thr consensus mot

DAP3.fn: As a component of the mitochondrial small ribosomal subunit, it plays a role in the translation of mitochondrial mRNAs. Involved in mediating interferon-gamma-induced cell death. Displays GTPase activity in vitro. .

DAXX.fn: Transcription corepressor known to repress transcriptional potential of several sumoylated transcription factors. Down-regulates basal and activated transcription.

DBF4.fn: Regulatory subunit for CDC7 which activates its kinase activity thereby playing a central role in DNA replication and cell proliferation. Required for progression of S phase.

DBR1.fn: Cleaves the 2'-5' phosphodiester linkage at the branch point of excised lariat intron RNA and converts them into linear molecules that can be subsequently degraded, thereby facilitating ribonucleotide turnover.

DCAF6.fn: Ligand-dependent coactivator of nuclear receptors. Enhance transcriptional activity of the nuclear receptors NR3C1 and AR. May function as a substrate receptor for CUL4-DDB1 E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase complex. .

DCLRE1B.fn: 5'-3' exonuclease that plays a central role in telomere maintenance and protection during S-phase. Participates in the protection of telomeres against non-homologous end-joining (NHEJ)-mediated repair, thereby ensuring that telomeres do not fuse.

DCTN1.fn: Part of the dynactin complex that activates the molecular motor dynein for ultra-processive transport along microtubules (By similarity).

DCTN2.fn: Part of the dynactin complex that activates the molecular motor dynein for ultra-processive transport along microtubules. In the dynactin soulder domain, binds the ACTR1A filament and acts as a molecular ruler to determine the length (By similarity).

DCTN3.fn: Part of the dynactin complex that activates the molecular motor dynein for ultra-processive transport along microtubules (By similarity). Together with dynein may be involved in spindle assembly and cytokinesis. .

DCTN4.fn: Part of the dynactin complex that activates the molecular motor dynein for ultra-processive transport along microtubules. .

DCTN5.fn: Part of the dynactin complex that activates the molecular motor dynein for ultra-processive transport along microtubules. .

DCTN6.fn: Part of the dynactin complex that activates the molecular motor dynein for ultra-processive transport along microtubules. .

DCUN1D5.fn: Contributes to the neddylation of all cullins by transferring NEDD8 from N-terminally acetylated NEDD8-conjugating E2s enzyme to different cullin C-terminal domain-RBX complexes which is necessary for the activation of cullin-RING E3 ubiquitin ligases (CRLs).

DDB1.fn: Involved in DNA repair and protein ubiquitination, as part of the UV-DDB complex and DCX (DDB1-CUL4-X-box) complexes, respectively.

DDN.fn: Promotes apoptosis of kidney glomerular podocytes. Podocytes are highly specialized cells essential to the ultrafiltration of blood, resulting in the extraction of urine and the retention of protein (By similarity). .
